reused_hash_contracts.subject: Request ownership
reused_hash_contracts.effect: The split native baseline already hoists upper-bound request search across layers. Shared/direct ownership must preserve repeated-boundary and last-row conventions.

reused_hash_contracts.subject: Hash source priority and sticky blockers
reused_hash_contracts.effect: Current chunk > known lookback > cache/pad; dead known entries block rather than fall through. Negative/dead blocking persists across later shifts.

reused_hash_contracts.subject: Layer/head output arithmetic
reused_hash_contracts.effect: Preserve INT64 multiply/XOR/modulo/offset behavior and full logical output demand. Shared input histories do not identify layer multipliers, head primes or output indices.

reused_hash_contracts.subject: Mapped-token cache publication
reused_hash_contracts.effect: History cache stores compressed/mapped token IDs or dead_id. Observed request-index -> cache-write -> hash order means fallback readers require that published generation, not an assumed old bank.

reused_hash_contracts.subject: KV owner rebinding
reused_hash_contracts.effect: Same live KV tensor object reuses history; an empty/unbound or replacement object resets it. Weak owner lifetime and zero initialization are part of the contract.

fusion_frontiers.decision: Compare shared request-index production with inlined/recomputed request mapping inside hash or a joint hash/lookup producer. Existing source explicitly separates the search for backend lowering; that is not proof of mathematical non-fusibility.
fusion_frontiers.budget: One existing INT32 request-index plane has4*T logical output bytes. Inlining can remove its storage/load edge but can repeat search across layers; charge actual producer/reader work once.
fusion_frontiers.gate: Preserve query partition, padding, selected invocation modes and native lowering acceptance. No probe is scheduled without a new critical-path or repeated-search decision.

fusion_frontiers.decision: Consider combining current token mapping/history writes with compatible upstream preparation or a proven same-kernel schedule; retain the publication edge required by fallback readers.
fusion_frontiers.budget: No removal of required mutable state updates merely because lookup output is cached. A cache-independent or disjoint-history read set can relax edges only when positively established.
fusion_frontiers.gate: Bind every written slot generation and every fallback reader. Ordinary thread-block execution order is not a replacement for the old kernel-completion boundary.

fusion_frontiers.decision: Use the existing UVA wrapper as the baseline: device-side ID widening already avoids a host-side INT32-to-INT64 copy. Direct layout writes or row caches retain pointer chunks, explicit vocabulary interval and local-head/padded-head semantics.
fusion_frontiers.budget: Do not invent a missing ID cast task or count construction pointer-table creation per token.
fusion_frontiers.gate: All code/scale mappings, output metadata and fixed group interpretation must remain valid through the final asynchronous reader.

Separate request search is an existing implementation/lowering choice. Keep joint production conditional rather than categorically excluding fusion.
Treat complete and partial release states separately. Existing global synchronization is a real lifetime edge; narrower retirement needs the full reader set.
Stop error-path research at the source contract relevant to mapping reuse; do not turn it into unrelated framework fault-injection work.

reused_lookup_counterexamples: Provided output [9,9] with one active unowned head and two total head columns becomes [0,9]. A generic full clear would change the second value.
For an unowned row whose safe row-zero table scale is E8M0 255, the final select emits +0. Replacing the select with multiplication by a zero ownership mask can emit NaN.
UVA MXFP8 performs one E8M0 load/decode per group already. Its per-value multiply does not imply 256 distinct scale reads.
